To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) A WD-WD binary, with a semi-major axis of 1-300 AU and an outer perturber, which orbits the WD-WD pair at a pericenter of 3-10x the inner semi-major axis, has a ~5% chance of experiencing a collision within 10^5 orbits.
(1) WD-WD binaries with a ~ 1-300 AU can experience a head-on collision with a high probability, and (2) this collision is likely to result in a type Ia SN.

(1) a WD-WD binary in a triple system is likely to experience a head-on collision with a pericenter distance of r_p < 4R_WDs within ~5 Gyorbits, and (2) such collisions are a possible source of type Ia SNEs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of a triple system consisting of a binary with two white dwarfs, and an outer stellar mass perturber.
a new mechanism to generate SNe Ia.
the evolution of a WD-WD binary that is perturbed by a stellar mass companion, and with the possibility of a head-on collision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a fraction of SNe Ia are likely to originate in WD-WD headon collisions, which are likely to be accompanied by gravitational wave emission.
the SNe Iacrate is likely to be as high as, and possibly higher than the SNe I rate.
WD-WD head on collisions are likely to be a significant source of SNe Ia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a triple with a WD-WD inner pair and an outer perturber can be considered a factory for WD-WD collisions.
a WD-WD binary with a=1-30AU, which is orbitted by a stellar mass perturber with r_{p, in} < 2a, is likely to experience a head-on collision.
the rate of SNe Ia is likely to be dominated by WD-WD collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a WD-WD system in a triple system is a dynamical system with a finite probability of a head-on collision.
a triple system is an efficient mechanism for transferring angular momentum from the outer perturber to the inner binary.

a perturbing outer companion with moderate pericenter (r_p ~ a) can efficiently transfer angular momentum to a binary, allowing the binary to scan the (equal energy, zero angular momentum) region in the phase space.
